items.title: Import a Super Simple Highlighter backup file into the library ('bring your highlights'), said on the listing and the comparison page
items.why: Super Simple Highlighter (200k users, local, free) documents a backup (beta) export holding every style and highlight location (dexterouslogic.com help, read 2026-10-04); its reviews say saved pages disappear and the help page admits no sync or backup. A refugee with that file can move across in one click — the only paid-vs-free argument we can make concrete. Build after library-backup-restore (same restore UI); first obtain a real backup file's layout (install the extension in the e2e Chromium, make two highlights, export) before writing the parser — never guess the format. Note 2026-10-04: Backup/Restore already exist on the library page but Restore calls replaceAll (wipes the current store) — build a pure merge (core, tested: newer page wins, highlights unioned by id) and use it for both Restore and this import, so a second machine's highlights survive. DONE 2026-10-04 (burn-down, 0.3.0): format read from the rival's own source (github.com/dexterouslogic/super-simple-highlighter, public archive: advanced.js export + db.js document fields — header line with the magic string, a style-definitions line, then a PouchDB replication-stream dump of {verb,match,date,range,className,text,title} docs); src/core/ssh-import.ts parses it (create docs minus the ones a delete doc names, page = our pageKey(match), colour by default class name or hue of a custom style, id ssh_<_id> so a second import is a no-op) with 4 tests; src/core/merge.ts is the pure merge (3 tests) and pages-storage.mergeInto uses it for Restore and the import; library page gains 'Import Super Simple Highlighter'; LISTING, AMO metadata, comparison page (new row + how-to), landing and welcome page say so. Not live until 0.3.0 is signed (ALERTS handoff).
items.proof: ≥ 1 import reported in a review or support mail within 60 days; installs after the listing line vs before

items.title: Import a Weava dashboard export (CSV/TXT) into the library — 'bring your highlights from Weava' on the listing and the comparison page
items.why: Weava (200k users, abandoned since Feb 2024, rating 2.9 on its last 100 reviews, 'highlights disappearing' the top complaint — web search 2026-10-05) is the refugee pool the whole comparison page targets, yet the page offers them no way across. Weava's own knowledge base (weavatools.atlassian.net, weavatools.com 'How to export your highlights and notes') documents a dashboard export to Word, Excel, CSV and plain text with resource URL, highlight and annotation. Both rivals that outrank us for 'weava alternative' built exactly this: Web Highlights ('How to import highlights from Weava') and Glasp ('Import Weava highlights to Glasp'). Same shape as the Super Simple import (text + URL + note → anchored by the quoted text, id weava_<hash> so a re-import is a no-op, merged through pages-storage.mergeInto). Verify the real CSV/TXT columns through the relay (weavatools.com + weavatools.atlassian.net added to the allowlist this run) before writing the parser; if the KB has no sample, parse by header names and fail loudly listing the headers seen. DONE 2026-10-05 (build 17:00, 0.4.0): the relay could not get a sample — Weava's KB page on the export redirects to an Atlassian login, app.weavatools.com does not answer, the Web Highlights and Glasp guides show only the dashboard steps, and weavatools.com's own how-to and manual say just 'Word, Excel, .csv or .txt' — so src/core/weava-import.ts reads the header row and maps columns by name (URL and highlight text required; note, title, folder→tag, colour by name or hex, date when present; id weava_<hash of url+quote+note> so a re-import is a no-op; merged through pages-storage.mergeInto) and refuses any other file listing the headers it saw, as planned. 8 tests (RFC 4180 reader, delimiter detection, header spellings, colour cells, stable ids, refusal text). Library gains 'Import Weava'; LISTING, AMO release notes and description, comparison page (row + the About Weava paragraph now tells refugees how to come across and to mail us the first line if the columns differ), landing and welcome page say so. Not live until 0.4.0 is signed (ALERTS handoff, supersedes the 0.3.0 one). First real file seen in support mail → fix the mapping the same day.
items.proof: ≥ 1 Weava import named in a review or support mail within 60 days; weava-alternative.html clicks → installs in Search Console/metrics after the line lands

items.title: Opt-in 'Highlight on every site' switch (optional <all_urls> host permission, asked once) beside the per-site model
items.why: Three of the 31 rival reviews in research/cws-reviews-2026-09-19.json ask for exactly this (Hypothesis ×2: 'a way to activate it for all webpages', 'wished it stayed active or automatically activated on every page'; Super Simple: 'can't figure out how to enable this extension on all websites by default … annoying to first enable on every new website') — the largest single ask after PDF and login. Our per-site switch is the privacy stance and stays the default; the manifest already declares optional_host_permissions for http/https, so a settings toggle that calls chrome.permissions.request({origins:['<all_urls>']}) and registers one content script for all sites is allowed by both stores as a user-triggered optional permission. Listing copy: 'on by default only where you switch it on; one setting turns it on everywhere'. e2e: toggle on, open a never-enabled site, highlight restores.
items.proof: the setting mentioned in a review or support mail; no store policy flag on the next review

items.title: Highlight inside iframes and shadow DOM: allFrames on the registered content script, shadow-root-aware range walking
items.why: Two rival reviews name it as the one gap in otherwise-liked products (Glasp: 'in some area like iFrame or Shadow DOM, i cant highlight'; Super Simple: 'really wish I could highlight in subframes'); Glasp's own listing text admits iframe/shadow-DOM gaps (2026-09-19 table). sites.ts registers content.js without allFrames, so a highlight attempted in an embedded reader or a web-component page does nothing. Fix: allFrames:true on registerContentScripts and injectNow (frame URL as the page key when it differs from the top page, so restores find it), composedPath/getRootNode in dom.ts so a selection inside an open shadow root anchors to its own text; store nothing extra. e2e: a fixture page with an iframe and a shadow-root paragraph, highlight both, reload, both restore.
items.proof: a fixture-backed e2e section passing; zero iframe/shadow complaints in the first reviews

items.title: Export: download one Markdown file per page (zip) for an Obsidian/Logseq vault, and a Readwise-import CSV — instead of clipboard only
items.why: Every rival a searcher sees ships a path into a notes app: Web Highlights (Notion, Obsidian, Capacities, Markdown/HTML/PDF), Glasp (Notion, Obsidian, Readwise, Roam, Logseq; MD/CSV/JSON), Readwise Highlighter (Reader → Obsidian/Notion/Logseq/Roam), Hypothesis (JSON/TXT/CSV/HTML) — web search 2026-10-05. Ours copies all pages' Markdown to the clipboard and saves a JSON backup; our listing's 'exports to Markdown' is the clipboard. Cheapest parity without any OAuth integration (which would break 'no account, no sync server'): (1) 'Download Markdown' — one .md per page named from the title, YAML front matter with url/date, zipped (a ~1 KB store-free zip writer or JSZip), dropped straight into a vault; (2) 'Download CSV for Readwise' in Readwise's documented import columns (Highlight, Title, Author, URL, Note, Location, Date — verify on docs.readwise.io through the relay; readwise.io added to the allowlist this run), which then flows to Notion/Obsidian/Anki through Readwise's own sync. Listing + comparison page: 'exports to Markdown files, JSON and Readwise CSV'.
items.proof: Readwise/Obsidian named in a review or support mail; downloads cannot be counted (no telemetry), so proof is listing conversions after vs before
